subject: SemanticAssuranceV2WorkflowService.aiSafetyClaimIndependenceCheck via assurance.ai-safety.claim-independence-check
coverage_notes: Seventh closure of Batch 5's disclosed broader-scope gap. The independence this operation enforces is structural, not merely documented: untested_claim_types is computed purely from SET MEMBERSHIP of claim_type strings actually present in submitted_claims -- the method never branches on any claim's decision value anywhere in its logic (in particular never on BUSINESS_CORRECTNESS's decision), so there is no code path by which a PASS on one claim type could cause a never-submitted type to read as tested. aiSafetyClaimIndependenceCheckBusinessCorrectnessPassAloneNeverImpliesAnySafetyClaim is the direct test of the named rule: submitting only BUSINESS_CORRECTNESS=PASS still leaves all 10 other claim types listed in untested_claim_types, proving the PASS carries zero positive weight for any other claim. Duplicate claim_type submissions are rejected outright (fail-closed, same discipline multiAgentCorroborationCheck already applies to duplicate agent conclusions) rather than silently overwritten or double-counted.
open_gap: Operates on caller-supplied claim submissions; there is no live safety/security test harness in this codebase that actually runs prompt-injection, RAG/tool-injection, exfiltration, privilege-escalation, etc. probes and produces these 10 decisions for real (same disclosed 'caller-supplied representation, not live system integration' pattern as every other Batch 5 broader-scope closure this session). A caller could submit all 11 claim types with fabricated PASS decisions and this operation would report all_claims_independently_evidenced=true -- it verifies COMPLETENESS of the claim set (nothing silently inferred), not the TRUTH of any individual submitted decision, which would require real adversarial test execution this codebase does not yet have.
